title: Structured outputs and bounded tool execution
notes: 3 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: The tool boundary is executable code. Define: A proposal becomes an action only after deterministic validation. Walk through: Tasks 3-5: valid JSON, invalid JSON, tool allowlist, numeric checks and a finite attempt budget. Ask: Why not execute a plausible tool name directly? Expected answer and boundary: A tool name is untrusted data. Unknown names must be rejected without dynamic evaluation or dispatch to arbitrary code. Visual purpose: show Untrusted JSON > Schema > Permission > Tool > Result. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Use exact fields and explicit types
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Use exact fields and explicit types. Define: Reject booleans, NaN, empty arrays and oversized arrays before calculation. Walk through: In Python isinstance(True,int) is true; the validator uses type(x) in (int,float) and a finite check. Ask: Why reject a Boolean in numeric readings? Expected answer and boundary: Its programming-language subtype does not establish the intended measurement meaning. The declared contract accepts numeric readings only. Visual purpose: show Exact keys | Known tool | Finite numbers | Size bound. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Numerical results need their own checks
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Numerical results need their own checks. Define: Valid inputs can still overflow a calculation; validate the result too. Walk through: Test the bounded mean implementation with large finite inputs; it must return a finite result or an explicit rejection. Ask: Does a valid schema prove the arithmetic is correct? Expected answer and boundary: No. Independently check arithmetic against small fixtures and reject nonfinite outputs rather than silently serializing them. Visual purpose: show Finite inputs > Stable aggregation > Finite output > Status. Walk through: Submit three proposals. The third must be budget_exhausted and must not invoke a tool. Ask: Why count rejected attempts? Expected answer and boundary: Otherwise repeated invalid proposals can loop forever without spending the nominal tool budget. Visual purpose: show Attempt 1 > Validate > Attempt 2 > Stop.
